value.a: A TICKET FOR DOCUMENT CHANGES WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED, and the reasoning is kept because the proposal was Akien's and it was a good instinct pointed at the wrong mechanism. His version: ticket every document change, which forces an orientation during /sail. Why it fails against BOTH measured instances: an orientation checks a change against the corpus, and in both cases the corpus was uniformly wrong, so orientation would have compared the edit to four artifacts that agreed with it and gone GREEN. That is a check that could not have failed, now carrying a seal — strictly worse than no check, because the next reader cites it as evidence. He agreed: 'i'm good with those. yes.'

WHAT ACTUALLY DETECTS THIS CLASS TODAY IS AKIEN READING THE DOCUMENT, twice out of two. That is not luck: he is the only oracle standing outside the corpus, and prose is what forces a claim into a shape he can recognise as wrong. The brief is therefore already an instrument and should be treated as one. This node does not replace that loop; it tries to catch the cheap half earlier so his reading is spent on the hard half.

cairn/machines/chart/ per-field provenance is PRECEDENT, not collision — same principle, different surface (a packet's field in flight vs an authored claim at rest). Borrow the shape; in-house prior art beats external.
